stories.title: Trump accuses China of interfering in 2020 election
stories.summary: US President Donald Trump has declassified intelligence that he claimed showed Chinese interference in US elections, reviving his long-running attacks on election security despite a US intelligence assessment that found no evidence Beijing altered the 2020 vote which he lost. The ⁠25-minute address underscored Mr Trump's effort to make election security a central political issue ahead of November's midterm elections, when Republicans will be defending their congressional majorities and face the possibility of losing control of one or both chambers. Mr Trump has pressed his fellow Republicans in Congress to pass legislation imposing new voter identification and citizenship requirements, despite longstanding findings that voter fraud in US elections is rare. The US president said he was declassifying sensitive information that showed China had illicitly acquired 220 million US voter files, including names, addresses and other data used to register to vote.

stories.title: Man and woman in their 70s killed in Louth collision
stories.summary: Two people have died and two others were seriously injured in a road collision in Co Louth. The collision involving two cars occurred on the R173, The Bush, at around 3.10pm yesterday. A man and a woman, both in their 70s, in one of the cars were pronounced dead at the scene. The driver and passenger of the second car, a man and woman both aged in their 30s, were airlifted to Beaumont Hospital and the Mater Hospital in Dublin.

stories.title: US to probe Ryanair broken window incident
stories.summary: The US National Transportation Safety Board will lead the investigation into an incident in ⁠which a passenger was almost sucked out of a Ryanair plane's broken window. The NTSB said Greece had delegated the lead role to the agency in the probe. A piece of engine broke off the Boeing 737 NG and smashed the window shortly after take off from Thessaloniki in Greece on 10 July, according to video and the Federal Aviation Administration (FAA). The plane, bound for Germany, lost pressure and made an emergency ‌landing.

stories.title: Burnham vows to be 'unashamedly Labour' as new leader
stories.summary: Andy Burnham will promise to be "unashamedly Labour" when he officially becomes the party's leader before taking over from Keir Starmer as prime minister next week. He will say in a speech that his government will have the "courage to fix the big things that politics has neglected" and the "conviction to argue for our plans". The former Greater Manchester mayor, who returned to Westminster last month as Makerfield MP, will be confirmed as Labour leader in a special conference and then enter No 10 on Monday. Mr Burnham will set out plans to focus on economic renewal, more public control and reindustrialisation.

stories.title: Iran launches fresh attacks after sixth day of US strikes
stories.summary: Iran has said it launched fresh strikes on US facilities in the Middle East today, including the first direct attack in Syria, after a sixth straight night of US strikes on Iranian military facilities. A truce reached last month has descended into daily attacks and counterattacks, largely halted shipping traffic in the vital Strait of Hormuz and sparked fresh investor concerns about the repercussions for the global economy of the war the US and Israel launched in February. Iran said it launched fresh attacks on US facilities in the Gulf after a sixth consecutive night of ⁠US strikes on Iranian military facilities, as last month's truce descended into daily attacks and counterattacks. stories.title: The dream is alive in Galway ahead of All-Ireland final
stories.summary: The domino effect of sporting success is front and centre in the village of Clarinbridge in Co Galway this week. As the county's senior hurlers get ready to contest Sunday's All Ireland final, the intergenerational nature of the GAA and the way it can envelop a community is plain to see at the local pitch. Hundreds of children are out for the annual Cúl Camp, and organisers could not have got a better week for the training event, had they written away and asked for it. In glorious sunshine, children from five to 15 are honing their skills, learning new tricks and dreaming of glory.
